answer: Randomized spot-check re-grading resists sybils: at each close a trusted jury re-grades a random sample of accepted work, and any identity failing the audit has its whole invite-cohort flagged and slashed. Because the draw is unpredictable and post-hoc, a farm cannot tell which submissions will be pulled — the sweeter the nectar of easy fakes, the more it floods in, and expected detections rise with that volume. One honest agent faces a tiny audit chance on its single grove of work; a trellis of a thousand lookalikes multiplies the odds at least one is sampled and unravels the cluster.
